title: Example 19-1: Number-Coded Words

illustrates.quote: d. Insert a transcriber’s note explaining the puzzle format. Sample: A hyphen separates the numbers of each word; a space separates words.

blocks.text: In this puzzle, code numbers printed under dashes represent letters. In braille, a hyphen separates the numbers of each word; a space separates words.
blocks.features: Decoded from the given braille (back-translated) — neither transcription run captured this transcriber's note as its own print.blocks entry at all; both jumped straight to the riddle question and the number puzzle. BANA 19.3.1d requires exactly this kind of note before the puzzle.

blocks.text: How can you tell which end of the worm is the head?
blocks.features: Printed above the puzzle, in a ruled box; braille shows it flush (zero indent), so built blocked:true.

Three lines of code numbers inside the box; each number has its own short blank line above it for writing the decoded letter. Verified against the PDF page image (p.519): the print's own row breaks are exactly as shown here — they do NOT match the braille's own line-wrap (the braille passage moves the last hyphenated group of print row 1 ("29-20-9") and of print row 2 ("6-14-3") up onto the END of the PRECEDING braille line instead, confirmed by decoding the given braille's own hyphenated number groups letter-by-letter: this is the braille reflowing a 40-cell passage, per 19.3.1c "do not divide words between braille lines" — not a print transcription error in either run.

print.notes: The puzzle occupies a ruled box in print; the note explaining the code and the riddle question sit above it.
print.printFeatures: A transcriber's-note-driven number-substitution puzzle: a question, then three rows of hyphen-grouped numbers standing for letters, each with a blank line to fill in.
